content:
This PR I think overall makes things a little better:

rss-bot said:

refactor(SimpleGraph): make completeGraph and emptyGraph abbrevs for ⊤ and ⊥ (mathlib4#23838)

define Top and Bot in-line for SimpleGraph and set completeGraph and emptyGraph as abbrev

Co-authored-by: FordUniver <61389961+FordUniver@users.noreply.github.com>

Authored-by: FordUniver (commit)

but should we just drop docs#SimpleGraph.completeGraph entirely? It's now an abbrev so it at least doesn't interfere with rw etc, but it still makes it confusing when naming lemmas.

I've admittedly not studied the graph theory part of mathlib much, but when looking over the diff of that PR, replacing the ⊤ and ⊥ with completeGraph and emptyGraph in theorem statements made them much easier for me to parse.

I'm a little surprised to see this changed. I'm pretty sure @Eric Wieser and @Yaël Dillies were both part of the discussion for the current design, where the point was to give some definitions for discoverability, and have the docstrings teach about top and bot.

A separate point is that there's a difference between semireducibility and instance reducibility, so having SimpleGraph.completeGraph defined first and then be used in the instance prevents it from being unnecessarily unfolded. It's like docs#SimpleGraph.IsSubgraph being a separate definition. (Pinging @Christoph Spiegel, since I see you asked about the seemingly backwards definition.) It's probably not a big deal in practice — and I can't say exactly what the difference will affect — but it was intentional.

It's not true that using an abbrev "doesn't interfere with rw" @Eric Wieser. The key matching means that for example you won't be able to rw [<- top_sup_eq] if the goal has completeGraph instead of \top. Maybe this will be relaxed this year if rw starts using discrimination trees.
Should we revert #23838 then?

It looks like #graph theory > bounded_lattice (simple_graph V) @ 💬 is the Zulip thread corresponding to !3#8330 which was the previous design. (It looks like I also put thumbs-up emojis agreeing with using top and bot instead of complete_graph and empty_graph...)

Kyle Miller said:

A separate point is that there's a difference between semireducibility and instance reducibility, so having SimpleGraph.completeGraph defined first and then be used in the instance prevents it from being unnecessarily unfolded.

I think we're pretty inconsistent about whether we do this; certainly, doing it leaves slightly confusing definitions around which confuse new users, sometimes to the point they feel urged to contribute and remove them!
(I agree there's a potential performance benefit)

Eric Wieser said:

Should we revert #23838 then?

If we do revert it, might I humbly request that someone expands the docstrings so that we don't end up changing it once again?

Sorry I missed this a year ago...

My original intent with #23838 was for combinatorialists to read completeGraph V / emptyGraph V throughout statements, goal state, and (possibly) lemma names, without having to think about
⊤ / ⊥ unless they want to. As far as I understand most people actually agree that this is sensible and the concern is about either needing to duplicate API or having the user rw when wanting to use order-based statements?

Kyle's point about rw [← top_sup_eq] is correct though even against current mathlib, so abbrev unfolding doesn't help there. Though notably this is only an issue for rewrites whose source pattern is ⊤/⊥ itself;
operator-position lemmas (top_sup_eq, le_top, sup_bot_eq, …) still work directly on completeGraph/ emptyGraph goals.

I am not familiar enough with mathlib to know what the best way to resolve this is without giving up the readability improvements for graph theorists. Duplicate API? Some index change to fix the rw? Something on the presentation layer?

Slight tangent: there is an argument to be made that completeGraph_eq_top and emptyGraph_eq_bot should have had their (previously necessary) @[simp] removed in #23838 to avoid unintended mid-proof rewriting to ⊤ / ⊥ . I drafted a branch with this that also updates the docstring. Happy to PR it.

For what it's worth, I'm in the opposite camp. I think ⊥ and ⊤ is one of those notational conventions that Mathlib should be exporting to wider mathematics, rather than us conforming to giving these two values unique names for each different structure.

IIUC the current convention is to use top/bot for naming and completeGraph/emptyGraph for spelling statements
cc @Yaël Dillies

/poll completeGraph/emptyGraph vs ⊤/⊥

completeGraph/emptyGraph
⊤/⊥
completeGraph/emptyGraph in names, ⊤/⊥ in statements
⊤/⊥ in names, completeGraph/emptyGraph in statements
⊤/⊥ in names, also in statements unless V can't be inferred (prefer completeGraph V over (⊤ : SimpleGraph V))

Violeta Hernández said:

For what it's worth, I'm in the opposite camp. I think ⊥ and ⊤ is one of those notational conventions that Mathlib should be exporting to wider mathematics, rather than us conforming to giving these two values unique names for each different structure.

So in your mind how should one denote 'the complete graph on nnn vertices' in an ordinary math paper?

Violeta Hernández said:

I think ⊥ and ⊤ is one of those notational conventions that Mathlib should be exporting to wider mathematics,

I think for this claim to be relevant to mathlib itself, we'd want to set an example by using these spellings for docs#Finset.univ and docs#Set.univ too, which is presumably controversial

I just remembered- it's worth mentioning that the meaning of ⊥ will change once SimpleGraph gets a verts : Set V field. Currently it's the graph with no edges on V, but after the refactor (no ETA) it'll be the graph with no edges and no vertices. Then we might still want to refer to graphs with no edges on a given set of vertices, but we probably won't have a lattice per vertex set but rather per vertex type, so it can't be ⊥.

James E Hanson said:

Violeta Hernández said:

For what it's worth, I'm in the opposite camp. I think ⊥ and ⊤ is one of those notational conventions that Mathlib should be exporting to wider mathematics, rather than us conforming to giving these two values unique names for each different structure.

So in your mind how should one denote 'the complete graph on nnn vertices' in an ordinary math paper?

as ⊤ and you can see n if you hover over it. (you can hover in ordinary math papers, right?)

Snir Broshi said:

I just remembered- it's worth mentioning that the meaning of ⊥ will change once SimpleGraph gets a verts : Set V field. Currently it's the graph with no edges on V, but after the refactor (no ETA) it'll be the graph with no edges and no vertices. Then we might still want to refer to graphs with no edges on a given set of vertices, but we probably won't have a lattice per vertex set but rather per vertex type, so it can't be ⊥.

Does that also affect the definition of the complete graph? Should the top of the lattice of vertex type V have the vertex set V? In this case this does not necessarily correspond to my intuition of the complete graph, where I would have imagined that the vertex set is untouched and all the edges are added.
Yes, I expect the lattice language to become close to useless once we add in vertex sets

Eric Wieser dijo:

Violeta Hernández said:

I think ⊥ and ⊤ is one of those notational conventions that Mathlib should be exporting to wider mathematics,

I think for this claim to be relevant to mathlib itself, we'd want to set an example by using these spellings for docs#Finset.univ and docs#Set.univ too, which is presumably controversial

For what it's worth, I'd be in favor of that too.

Snir Broshi said:

I just remembered- it's worth mentioning that the meaning of ⊥ will change once SimpleGraph gets a verts : Set V field. Currently it's the graph with no edges on V, but after the refactor (no ETA) it'll be the graph with no edges and no vertices. Then we might still want to refer to graphs with no edges on a given set of vertices, but we probably won't have a lattice per vertex set but rather per vertex type, so it can't be ⊥.

Yaël Dillies said:

Yes, I expect the lattice language to become close to useless once we add in vertex sets

That seems relevant to me. I think ⊥ as the "empty graph" in the sense of a graph without vertices and edges makes sense. It e.g. occurs as the unit in flag algebra terms where one commonly denotes it ∅. It is the use of ⊥ and ⊤ for the graph with no / all edges on a given specific vertex set that doesn't quite mesh with me. At least in the parts of graph theory that I am familiar with, the lattice structure on a specific vertex set is not what one usually cares about.

But I think this is an issue that is inherent in defining a graph with a vertex type instead of a vertex set. So probably it makes sense to defer any decision until the vertex set refactor is through (or to already consider any preferences voiced here in there). But I would expect that after that refactor the distinction of when one actually talks about bot and top in the lattice structure vs. when one talks about an empty or a complete graph on a specific vertex set in graph theory terms becomes more clear.
Oh, are we planning to redefine SimpleGraph as a single type instead of a family indexed by V? (I'm completely in favor, I just wasn't aware)

Violeta Hernández said:

Oh, are we planning to redefine SimpleGraph as a single type instead of a family indexed by V? (I'm completely in favor, I just wasn't aware)

Wait how would that work? That sounds completely impossible due to size considerations.
...am I misunderstanding the proposal?

It'll still have a type, just also a carrier set inside.

structure SimpleGraph (V : Type*) where
  verts : Set α
  Adj : α → α → Prop
  ...

Basically promoting docs#SimpleGraph.Subgraph (G := ⊤) to be the new docs#SimpleGraph
Oh. Well, I never claimed I understood the design behind graphs in Mathlib.
